title: Lambda is borrowing $917m to buy chips from the company that invests in it
excerpt: Lambda is selling a $917m leveraged loan to fund a contract with Nvidia, which is also its investor, supplier and largest customer. Books hit $2bn.
content_html:
Lambda is selling a $917 million leveraged loan to finance a chip purchase, Bloomberg reported on Monday. Jeannine Amodeo, Paula Seligson and Gowri Gurumurthy broke the story. The money pays for GPUs and other infrastructure as part of a contract with Nvidia, according to a person with knowledge of the matter. Morgan Stanley leads the transaction.

Lambda Compute II LLC and Lambda Cloud Canada Inc will issue the debt. A lender call opened at 10:30am New York time on Monday. Commitments fall due on Thursday. Order books had reached nearly $2 billion after a pre-marketing effort.

Bloomberg frames the risky debt market as a new front in the borrowing binge funding the AI buildout. Its own compiled data puts global AI-linked borrowing at nearly $600 billion since last year. Lambda belongs to the group of firms known as neoclouds, which rent out access to microchips and other AI infrastructure.

The circle closes on itself

Start with who sits on the other side of the contract. Nvidia already held an investment in Lambda. It also supplies every chip Lambda runs, because the company uses Nvidia silicon exclusively.

Then it went further. In September 2025 Nvidia agreed to lease GPUs back from Lambda, in a $1.3bn four-year deal covering 10,000 servers plus a $200m contract for 8,000 more. RCR Wireless reported that the arrangement made Nvidia its largest customer, worth roughly $1.5bn across 18,000 servers.

So Nvidia plays four roles at once. Investor, supplier, biggest tenant, and now counterparty to the contract a $917m loan exists to fund.

The shape is familiar. Google built the same loop around its own TPUs, guaranteeing rent for data centres that buy its chips to serve Anthropic. The Bank for International Settlements flagged the pattern in June, warning that an AI investment collapse could disrupt credit markets on the scale of 2008.

The BIS singled out chipmakers taking equity stakes in firms that then commit to buying chips from those same investors. The terms of such deals, it said, “are typically poorly disclosed, with risks of the same asset being pledged multiple times.”

The venue matters more than the number

$917m looks small next to the sums moving through AI infrastructure. The venue does not. This deal lands in the institutional leveraged loan market, where investors buy the debt of companies rated below investment grade.

CoreWeave opened that door in April. Bloomberg called its $3.1bn deal the first of its kind to finance chips in the institutional loan market. CoreWeave then sold debt backed by customer contracts, including one with OpenAI, in May. A later deal backed by different contracts forced it to pay a hefty yield, which pushed its borrowing costs up sharply.

Compare the alternative route. Nebius raised a $775m GPU-backed facility in July at SOFR plus 2.50 percentage points, roughly 6.8%. Banks syndicated that one. An investment-grade customer contract sat behind it, throwing off cash flows that covered more than 100% of the capital expenditure.

Lambda pays as much as 3.75 percentage points over the benchmark rate, at a discounted price of 99 cents on the dollar. Same collateral class, different market, higher cost.

The terms name the nervous party

Read the structure and you can see what lenders demanded. The loan matures in 4.4 years. Institutional loans usually run seven.

It also amortises fully, so the debt repays over roughly four years rather than landing as a lump at the end. Bloomberg notes that amortisation ranks among the protections investors have been seeking. Here it means lenders carry no refinancing risk at all.

A call-protection clause adds a penalty if Lambda redeems the debt early. Bloomberg describes that combination as closer to a bond deal than a loan.

Those features do one specific job. They shorten the window in which a GPU has to keep earning. TNW noted the open question when Nebius borrowed in July. The whole asset class rests on residual value assumptions that nobody in this industry has had to test yet. A four-year amortising schedule sidesteps that question rather than answering it.

What Lambda actually is

Machine learning engineers founded the company in 2012, working out of the Noisebridge hackerspace in San Francisco’s Mission District. It now calls itself an AI-only company and builds modular AI factories with power, liquid cooling and high-bandwidth interconnects, at what it describes as gigawatt scale. Its mission statement promises to “make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone in America the power of superintelligence.”

A management overhaul followed a $1.5bn Series E in November 2025. Lambda named Michel Combes chief executive in May, after his runs at Sprint, SoftBank International and Alcatel-Lucent. Former AT&T Communications boss John Donovan became chairman. Co-founders Stephen and Michael Balaban moved to chief technology officer and chief product officer. The company targets 3GW of AI compute under management by 2030.

Microsoft signed a multibillion-dollar agreement with Lambda last November to deploy tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs, CNBC reported. Lambda has held preliminary discussions with bankers about a public listing. It sells only in North America, and it has started building its own data centres rather than renting space in other people’s.

What the deal does not settle

Investors clearly want the paper. Order books of nearly $2bn against a $917m loan point to real demand, and the amortising structure shows they went in with their eyes open.

Several things stay unresolved. Lambda and Morgan Stanley did not respond to Bloomberg’s requests for comment. The detail tying the debt to an Nvidia contract comes from an unnamed person. Lambda’s revenue and loss figures sit behind paywalled reporting, so no audited number exists in public.

The wider market has also turned fussier. Loan investors started pushing back this month as fear rose, Bloomberg reported. Big Tech alone has lined up $350bn of AI debt over five years, and private credit keeps stacking more on top. Blue Owl’s Stack Infrastructure is chasing a $5.9bn data centre loan of its own.

Lambda leaves lenders one question, and it has nothing to do with chips. Nvidia sits on both sides of this trade. If AI demand holds, that reads as alignment. If it slips, the same fact reads as concentration, and the loan matures long before anyone finds out which.

content_html_zh:
据彭博社周一报道，Lambda 正在出售一笔 9.17 亿美元的杠杆贷款，为芯片采购提供资金。 Jeannine Amodeo、Paula Seligson 和 Gowri Gurumurthy 报道了这个故事。 据一位知情人士透露，这笔钱用于支付 GPU 和其他基础设施的费用，这是与 Nvidia 签订的合同的一部分。 摩根士丹利主导了此次交易。

Lambda Compute II LLC 和 Lambda Cloud Canada Inc 将发行该债务。 纽约时间周一上午 10 点 30 分，贷款人电话会议开始。 承诺将于周四到期。 经过前期营销努力后，订单已达到近 20 亿美元。

彭博社将高风险债务市场视为人工智能建设融资狂欢的新战线。 其自己编制的数据显示，自去年以来，全球与人工智能相关的借款已接近 6000 亿美元。 Lambda 属于 Neoclouds 公司集团，该集团出租微芯片和其他人工智能基础设施的访问权限。

圆圈自行闭合

从合同另一方的人开始。 Nvidia 已经投资了 Lambda。 它还供应 Lambda 运行的所有芯片，因为该公司只使用 Nvidia 芯片。

然后它更进一步。 2025 年 9 月，Nvidia 同意从 Lambda 租回 GPU，签订了一项价值 13 亿美元的四年期协议，涵盖 10,000 台服务器以及价值 2 亿美元的合同，涵盖 8,000 台服务器。 RCR Wireless 报道称，这一安排使 Nvidia 成为其最大客户，其 18,000 台服务器价值约 15 亿美元。

所以英伟达同时扮演四个角色。 投资者、供应商、最大的租户，现在是合同的对手方，需要一笔 9.17 亿美元的贷款来资助。

形状很熟悉。 谷歌围绕自己的 TPU 构建了相同的循环，为购买其芯片为 Anthropic 提供服务的数据中心提供租金保障。 国际清算银行 (Bank for International Settlements) 在 6 月份指出了这一模式，警告称人工智能投资崩溃可能会产生 2008 年规模的扰乱信贷市场。

国际清算银行特别指出，芯片制造商持有公司股权，然后承诺从这些投资者那里购买芯片。 报告称，此类交易的条款“通常披露不充分，存在同一资产被多次质押的风险”。

场地比人数更重要

与人工智能基础设施的资金相比，9.17 亿美元显得微不足道。 场地没有。 该交易涉及机构杠杆贷款市场，投资者购买评级低于投资级别的公司的债务。

CoreWeave 在四月份打开了这扇门。 彭博社称其 31 亿美元的交易是机构贷款市场上首笔同类融资交易。 随后，CoreWeave 在 5 月份出售了由客户合同支持的债务，其中包括与 OpenAI 的合同。 后来的一项由不同合同支持的交易迫使其支付高额收益率，这导致其借贷成本急剧上升。

比较替代路线。 Nebius 在 7 月份筹集了 7.75 亿美元的 GPU 支持融资，SOFR 上涨了 2.50 个百分点，约为 6.8%。 银行联合了这一点。 其背后有一份投资级客户合同，产生的现金流覆盖了超过 100% 的资本支出。

Lambda 支付的费用比基准利率高出 3.75 个百分点，折扣价为 99 美分。 相同抵押品类别，不同市场，成本较高。

这些术语命名了紧张的一方

阅读结构，您可以了解贷方的要求。 贷款期限为 4.4 年。 机构贷款通常为七。

它还可以全额摊销，因此债务将在大约四年内偿还，而不是最后一次性全部偿还。 彭博社指出，摊销属于投资者一直寻求的保护措施之一。 这意味着贷方根本不承担再融资风险。

如果 Lambda 提前赎回债务，赎回保护条款会增加处罚。 彭博社称这种组合更接近于债券交易而不是贷款。

这些功能只完成一项特定的工作。 它们缩短了 GPU 必须持续盈利的时间窗口。 Nebius 在 7 月份借款时，TNW 注意到了这个悬而未决的问题。 整个资产类别都基于残值假设，而该行业中尚未有人测试过该假设。 四年期摊销时间表回避了这个问题，而不是回答它。

Lambda 到底是什么

机器学习工程师于 2012 年创立了该公司，在旧金山 Mission 区的 Noisebridge 黑客空间工作。 该公司现在称自己为一家专注于人工智能的公司，并以千兆瓦级规模建造了配备电源、液体冷却和高带宽互连的模块化人工智能工厂。 其使命宣言承诺“让计算像电力一样无处不在，让美国每个人都拥有超级智能的力量。”

2025 年 11 月，在完成 15 亿美元的 E 轮融资后，进行了管理层改革。 Lambda 于 5 月任命米歇尔·库姆斯 (Michel Combes) 为首席执行官，此前他曾在 Sprint、软银国际 (SoftBank International) 和阿尔卡特朗讯 (Alcatel-Lucent) 任职。 AT&T Communications 前老板约翰·多诺万 (John Donovan) 出任董事长。 联合创始人斯蒂芬·巴拉班和迈克尔·巴拉班晋升为首席技术官和首席产品官。 该公司的目标是到 2030 年管理 3GW 的人工智能计算。

据 CNBC 报道，去年 11 月，微软与 Lambda 签署了一项价值数十亿美元的协议，部署数万个 Nvidia GPU。 Lambda 已与银行家就公开上市进行了初步讨论。 它只在北美销售，并且已经开始建立自己的数据中心，而不是租用别人的空间。

交易未解决的问题

投资者显然想要这份文件。 9.17 亿美元贷款的近 20 亿美元订单表明了实际需求，而摊销结构表明他们对此是睁大眼睛的。

有几件事仍未解决。 Lambda 和摩根士丹利没有回应彭博社的置评请求。 将债务与英伟达合同挂钩的细节来自一位不愿透露姓名的人士。 Lambda 的收入和亏损数据来自付费报告，因此公开的审计数据不存在。

更广泛的市场也变得更加挑剔。 据彭博社报道，随着担忧情绪加剧，贷款投资者本月开始推迟贷款。 仅大型科技公司就在五年内背负了 3500 亿美元的人工智能债务，而私人信贷的债务不断增加。 Blue Owl 的 Stack Infrastructure 正在寻求 59 亿美元的数据中心贷款。

Lambda 给贷方留下了一个问题，而且它与芯片无关。 英伟达处于这场交易的双方。 如果人工智能需求成立，那就可以理解为一致。 如果出现下滑，同样的事实也被解读为集中化，贷款早在任何人发现之前就到期了。
